source.title: Apply Operations to Make All Array Elements Equal to Zero

teaching.hint: Once an early position has become zero, where could a later operation that still changes it begin?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: After earlier positions are fixed at zero, the effective value at the current position forces exactly how many length-k operations must start there; an earlier start would disturb a finished position, and a later start cannot reach it.
solution_outline.approach: Scan left to right, tracking the total decrements from active windows. If the current effective value is negative or a required window no longer fits, return false. Otherwise apply that many operations starting here as one deferred range update. Return true after every position is zero.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Before each index, all earlier positions are exactly zero and the running adjustment equals the sum of active forced window decrements. A scheduled cancellation removes each adjustment immediately after its length-k window ends.
solution_outline.correctness: Every future operation affecting the current position must start here: starts earlier would also alter an already-zero earlier position, while starts later miss it. Thus a positive effective value forces that many operations, and a negative value or missing window proves impossibility. Deferred updates have the same effect as those operations, so induction over positions establishes the final answer.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space using deferred range updates, for n up to 100,000.
solution_outline.pitfall: A total sum divisible by k is insufficient for feasibility; the forced windows can over-decrease a later element.

common_wrong_turns: Apply each repeated operation to all k elements literally
Assume divisibility of the sum decides feasibility
source_fidelity_notes: Example transcripts were omitted; exactly-k contiguous operations, repeated use, nonnegative initial values, bounds, and all-zero objective were retained.
